verdict_reason: The three notification-keyed document routes now check ownership, but the upload-id routes stay unscoped, the new checks are untested, and the header constant has two names.

todos.issue: Only the three /notifications/{ref}/... document routes check the owning organisation (lines 93, 123, 174). The upload-id routes the frontend also calls for a trader (claim :144, get :195, delete :216, downloadFile :261; services/document-uploads/real.js:28,72,84,94) take no organisation header and are outside TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter (shouldNotFilter skips any path not starting /notifications). A trader in organisation B who holds an upload id from organisation A's notification can read its metadata, stream the file, delete it, or claim it into A's notification - against the story's 'other organisations cannot see or change our consignments' and the AC that reading or changing another organisation's notification returns 404.
todos.fix: Must: every trader-facing document route, including those keyed by upload id, returns 404 when the upload belongs to a notification outside the caller's organisation, and rejects a request with no organisation id. One way: require the organisation header on claim/get/delete/file, resolve the upload's notificationRef in DocumentService, call notificationService.requireTraderAccess(ref, organisationId) before acting, and extend the filter's path match to /document-uploads (keeping scan-results, the cdp-uploader callback, excluded).

todos.issue: The new ownership checks at lines 93, 123 and 174 have no test that fails without them. DocumentControllerTest stubs requireTraderAccess to do nothing for every test (@BeforeEach allowTraderNotificationAccess, DocumentControllerTest.java:77-79), and DocumentControllerIT has no organisation set-up at all, so deleting any of the three calls leaves the suite green. The AC asks for tests showing organisation A cannot see or change organisation B's notification.
todos.fix: Must: for register, session and list, a test sends organisation B's id for a notification owned by organisation A, asserts 404, and goes red if the requireTraderAccess call is removed. One way: in DocumentControllerIT, seed a notification with organisationId A and call each route with header B; assert 404 and that no upload session was written for register.

todos.issue: The organisation header has two names for one value: DocumentController reads NotificationController.HEADER_ORGANISATION_ID (lines 34, 88, 119, 172), which is only an alias for TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter.ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER (NotificationController.java:44), while DocumentControllerTest sends TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter.ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER. The document package now depends on the notification controller for a constant the filter owns.
todos.fix: Must: one constant names the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and every controller and test refers to it by that one name. One way: import TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter.ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER here (and in NotificationController), delete the HEADER_ORGANISATION_ID alias, and drop the NotificationController import.

todos.issue: The public contract of register, session and list is now out of date: register's OpenAPI responses (lines 80-84) list no 404 though requireTraderAccess now throws NotFoundException for another organisation's notification, none of the three documents the 400 for a missing organisation header, and their Javadoc (lines 69-75, 100-106, 156-161) has no @param for the new organisationId parameter.
todos.fix: Must: each of the three operations documents the organisation header, the 404 for a notification outside the caller's organisation, and the 400 for a missing header, in both the OpenAPI annotations and the Javadoc @param list. One way: add @ApiResponse(responseCode = "404") to register, a 400 response to session and list, and an @param organisationId line to each Javadoc.
